title: AgentDock — grounded plan-execute agent platform
summary: Code walks a catalog-grounded tool procedure with checkpoints; the model fills each step; a deny-by-default effect gate holds external actions for exact human approval that resumes the run.
autonomy: Hybrid (Ch1, Ch24). Plan creation: model drafts, user approves in chat. Run execution: code owns the procedure loop, budgets and stop reasons; model fills arguments per step with a bounded recovery loop on failure. External effects: act-with-approval per agent setting; reads auto-run.
key_decisions: Plan-execute: code walks the grounded procedure, model fills steps (Ch13, Ch24)
Approve exact actions; approval resumes a checkpointed run (Ch49, Ch23)
Deny-by-default effect gate by effect class, not regex vibes (Ch48)
One agent per run; planner and runner are roles, not a crew (Ch31)
Tool results and event payloads are data, never instructions (Ch47)
Checkpointed state machine beats the 300s serverless ceiling (Ch19)
rationale: Hybrid over free agent: after grounding, the steps ARE enumerable, so the orchestrator executes them in code and the model only fills arguments and interprets results; a bounded recovery loop handles the genuinely observation-dependent part (Ch24, Ch13).
Procedure validator in code, not model: every procedure step's tool slug is checked against the live catalog before save; a plan referencing a nonexistent operation cannot be saved (Ch7, Ch48).
Single agent: planner, step executor and reflector are model roles coordinated by code; no measured shortfall justifies agent-to-agent handoffs (Ch31).

Effect gate replaces the name-regex approval intercept: every proposed call is classified (read / internal write / external message / money / delete) from catalog metadata plus an override table; external classes require approval unless the owner opted out per agent; unknown class denies (Ch48, Ch65).

Approval as durable interrupt: the run checkpoints after every completed step; approving executes the exact held call and resumes remaining steps — today's replay-only approval silently drops post-action steps (Ch23, Ch49).

Memory split: episodic (run logs), semantic (reflected facts with provenance), procedural (proven procedure, replayed first); reflection deletes disproven facts; memory never changes permissions (Ch18, Ch19).
Webhook idempotency: events deduped by webhook-id before dispatch so Composio redelivery cannot double-run an agent (Ch14, Ch53).
Built-in web research tools ride the same gate as Composio tools, classified read-only (Ch11).
trust_boundaries: Browser to API: better-auth session plus zod-typed request bodies on every route; ownership checked on every read and write (Ch51).
Composio webhook to router: HMAC signature verification plus webhook-id dedupe; payload stored as untrusted event data (Ch47, Ch53).

Model proposal to tool dispatch: per-agent allowlist (procedure tools + read-only discovery set) that fails closed, then the effect policy gate; unknown tools and unknown effect classes deny (Ch29, Ch48).
Tool results, web content and event payloads to model: labelled untrusted data in the conversation, never system-prompt content; injection-defense rule in every run (Ch9, Ch47).
failure_handling: Budgets: per-run step budget, bounded per-step recovery retries, token budget per run; named stop reasons recorded on every run: DONE, FAILED, STEP_BUDGET, TOKEN_BUDGET, LOOP_DETECTED, WAITING_APPROVAL, DENIED, SKIPPED_PRECONDITION (Ch14).
Every tool call has a timeout and one result envelope; errors classified transient (retry once with backoff) or permanent (scope/permission errors never retried) (Ch14, Ch53).
Approvals are single-use and expire after 72h to no-effect plus a dashboard notice; execution re-checks connection and ownership at approve time (Ch49).
Cron backoff for agents with missing connections; webhook redelivery deduped by event id; duplicate in-run calls served from result cache (Ch53).
Checkpoint after every completed step keyed by run id; resume never repeats a completed side effect (Ch19, Ch23).
hitl: External effects (messages, posts, money, deletes) on agents set to ask-first: owner approves the exact tool call with full payload shown; approval executes that call and resumes the run (Ch49).
Plan approval: no agent exists until the owner approves the grounded plan in the builder chat (Ch49).
Training gate: an agent cannot be scheduled until one training run verifiably succeeds (Ch56).
evals: Golden set from reality: every successful training run is frozen as a golden case (procedure + expected trace shape); weekly replay detects drift and flags agents whose proven path broke (Ch42).

Dimensions traced separately: task success (outcome verifier), tool accuracy (procedure adherence), efficiency (steps, tokens), safety (zero unapproved external effects, checked against the audit log) (Ch41).
Red-team ledger: injection-in-email cases, scope-error cases, empty-result cases re-run after every RULES or gate change (Ch50).
Release gate for platform changes: replay the golden set before deploy; PROMOTE only with zero safety regressions (Ch45).
risks: Prompt injection in emails or web content steering tool calls: effect gate + approval on external effects + injection rules; owner: platform (Ch47).
Composio dependency (auth, triggers, execution): abstracted tool-plane interface; exit path is per-app direct OAuth or vendor MCP servers; owner: founder (Ch57).
Serverless time ceiling truncating long runs: checkpointed resume; runs continue on next invocation; owner: platform (Ch51).
Approval rubber-stamping: full payload shown, audit sampling; owner: product (Ch49).
Memory poisoning from hallucinated IDs: reflection validates against trace, deletes disproven facts, caps size; owner: platform (Ch18).
non_goals: Arbitrary code execution or generic shell tools
Self-hosted per-app OAuth (stays on managed auth in this phase)
